To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
KNAT6 and STM redundantly contribute to the maintenance of meristematic cells and organ boundaries.

KNAT6 and STM redundantly contribute to the maintenance of meristematic function and organ separation, that this function is linked to the activity of CUC genes, and that KNAT2 does not play such a role.
KNAT6 is a homeobox gene that contributes to the maintenance of SAM activity and the formation of boundaries between organs during embryogenesis and that this function is independent of KNAT2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying meristematic activity and organ separation.
the identification of the function of two members of the Arabidopsis homeobox gene family and their contribution to the development of the shoot apices and organ separation.
the identification and characterization of the Arabidopsis thalina gene KNAT6.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the KNAT6 protein is a transcriptional regulator that acts redundantly with STM during the maintenance of SAM and organ separation in the embryo and during the maintenance of meristematic function and organ separation in adult plants.
KNAT6 is required to maintain SAM activity and to establish organ boundaries, whereas KNAT2 has no such role.
KNAT6 is a homeobox gene involved in the establishment and maintenance of meristem function, and in organ separation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KNAT6 is involved in the maintenance of the meristem activity and the organ separation in the embryo and in the post-embryonic development.
KNAT6 plays an important role in the maintenance of the SAM and in organ separation in the embryo and seedling, and this function is linked to the modulation activity of CUC1/2.
KNAT6 is a homeodomain protein involved in the maintenance of the SAM, organ separation and embryogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KNAT family is composed of genes that have evolved distinct functions.
the KNAT6 protein is involved in the establishment of the boundaries between the different parts of the plant body.
the KNAT6 gene plays a crucial role in the maintenance of the SAM activity and in the separation of organs in the embryo.
